first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, so simplifying onboarding is the most direct intervention with evidence of durable time-to-value and activation benefits. I want to verify that evidence and compare it with the competitor-response case for promotional pricing before committing. A small guarded test should measure qualified activation, retained usage, and downstream pipeline—not just completion—because simplification or discounts could increase low-quality conversions.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding, since completion is down 4% and the verified prior result showed a 13% completion lift, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and a 3% improvement in 30-day retention. This is more aligned with sustainable qualified revenue than promotional pricing: the verified discount increased qualified revenue 18% short term but reduced 30-day retention 12% and failed at the first renewal cycle. Evaluate activation, time-to-value, qualified pipeline or revenue, and 30-day retention, with a stop condition if downstream quality or retention declines.
